note: Signature codes extracted from the drawing sheets. Per-device grouping is approximate — designators are printed upright and codes rotated, so they come from separate OCR passes. Treat the codes as reliable and the grouping as a hint. That caveat applies to 'byDevice' only. 'pinMap' is different: it is read by eye off the four typeset figures on DP-156 sheet 1 Side B, which print each signature against the device pin it belongs to, so both the code and the pin are exact there.
shared: Red Baron uses the same Auxiliary Math Box PCB as Battlezone (Atari 035678-01), so a known-good board from either game checks the other. Device positions, read off DP-156 sheet 3 Side B and cross-checked against the Figure 1 test-point map on sheet 1 Side B: the six microcode PROMs are M1 (036175), L1 (036176), K1 (036177), J1 (036178), H1 (036179) and F1 (036180); the entry PROM is B1 (036174, 82S123); the microcode program counter is E1 and D1 (two 74LS161s); its address latch is C1 (74LS374); and the ALU is four Atari 137004-001 bit slices at K2, F2, H/J2 and D/E2. An earlier version of this note listed the slices as J2, F/H2, E2 and C/D2 and left M1 out of the device list -- both came from the approximate OCR grouping described above.
probeNote: Codes marked with an asterisk on the drawing are taken with a 1k resistor between the signature analyser's data probe and +5V. Without it those readings do not reproduce. The note appears only on the 2nd printing of DP-156-03.

procedure.board: Auxiliary PCB 035678-01 (shared by Battlezone and Red Baron)
procedure.source: DP-156 sheet 1 Side B, 'Auxiliary PCB Signature Analysis Procedure'
procedure.equipment: Atari CAT (Computer-Assisted Troubleshooter), Kurz-Kasch Signature II, or HP 5004A signature analyser. Note on the drawing: of two Kurz-Kasch Signature IIs tried, different START, STOP and CLOCK settings were required -- note your own settings while testing a known-good board.
procedure.harness: Atari P/N A036836-01, or make one: Molex 7-circuit housing 09-05-7071 x1, 12-circuit housing 09-50-7121 x3, terminals 08-50-0106 x18, three jumper wires with hook connectors on each end, and a 1k-1.5k quarter-watt pull-up resistor.
procedure.setup: Set the Battlezone self-test switch ON; after about three seconds the monitor should show the self-test pattern. Then jumper a 1k resistor between the two test points on the Analog Vector-Generator PCB to ground five times, or until the video display is blank.

tests.1: Plug the harness Test #1 connector onto the SA header on the Auxiliary PCB. Jumper pin 1 of IC B6 on the Analog Vector-Generator PCB to ground -- this holds RESET to the microprocessor. Verify by probing the +5V test point: it must read CC34. Then probe per Figure 1. The 1k-1.5k resistor runs from +5V on the Auxiliary PCB to the probe tip for this test.
tests.2A: Remove the resistor from the probe, plug the Test #2 connector, remove the jumper from pin 1 of B6, verify at the +5V test point, then probe per Figure 2A.
tests.2B: Test #2 connector still plugged; remove the jumper from pin 6 of B6 on the Analog Vector-Generator PCB, verify a signature of 72A2, then probe per Figure 2B.
tests.3: Plug the Test #3 connector, remove the jumper from pin 6 of B6, verify, then probe per Figure 3.

procedure.isolating: Find the failing test point on sheet 3 Side B and identify the IC the signature is output from, then check all of that IC's inputs. If every input is correct, the IC is the fault -- but first pull the PCB and check the traces common to that pin, top and bottom, for a short to another trace. If an input is wrong, move to the IC sourcing that input and repeat, working upstream until the failing IC is isolated.
procedure.caveat: The verification signatures quoted here for tests 2A, 2B and 3 were read from a scan and only 72A2 and the Test #1 CC34 were confirmed at high magnification. Read the sheet before relying on the others.
